name: Le Havre
desc: The second largest seaport in France. Visitors' pontoon in the first of the two marinas. Masts can be unstepped/raised here.

name: Honfleur
desc: Artists and photographers compete to capture the Vieux Bassin where visiting boats secure. Packed with art galleries, souvenir shops and tourists. Church of St Catherine built of wood by local shipbuilders. Very crowded in high season.

name: Caudebec-en-Caux
desc: Picturesque small town with interesting Musée de la Marine de Seine. Landing stage can be used free of charge. Victor Hugo's daughter drowned nearby.

name: Duclair
desc: Attractive small town with sailing club. Pontoon (free of charge if not required by tourist boats). Check with Hôtel de Ville.

name: Rouen
desc: Impressive run-in to the centre of Rouen, dominated by the great Gothic Cathedral. Medieval market square where Joan of Arc was burned. Port de Plaisance with excellent facilities. The old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Les Andelys
desc: Community dates back to the Romans. Overlooking the Seine is the ruined Château Gaillard, built by Richard I of England in 1196-7. Moorings available.

name: Vernon
desc: Medieval tower of the old castle remains standing. Good range of moorings. Monet's garden at Giverny is just a few kilometres away.

name: Mantes-la-Jolie
desc: Much industrial development in the area. The church of Notre-Dame de Mantes, a Romanesque edifice, is interesting. Moorings available.

name: Conflans-Ste-Honorine
desc: Barge capital of France – almost always a large congregation of barges moored here. The Musée de la Batellerie (Inland Waterways Museum) is here.

name: Paris – Port de l'Arsenal
desc: The Port de Plaisance de Paris-Arsenal is just off Place de la Bastille, 3km upriver of Notre Dame. Excellent base for exploring Paris. Advance booking essential. The boat glides beneath the Pont Neuf in the shadows of Notre Dame on the Île de la Cité.

name: Montereau-Fault-Yonne
desc: Junction of the Seine and Yonne rivers. Napoleon defeated the Austrians here in 1814. Comfortable moorings in the port de plaisance.

name: Auxerre
desc: Attractive old city on a hill above the Yonne. Cathedral of St Etienne. Good moorings in the port de plaisance. A good place to provision.

name: Joigny
desc: Attractive hillside town in the Yonne valley. Fine Romanesque church. Comfortable moorings.

name: Meaux
desc: Cathedral city on the Marne. Cathedral of St-Etienne is impressive. Comfortable moorings. Famous for Brie cheese.

name: Épernay
desc: The champagne capital. Avenue de Champagne is lined with the great champagne houses – Moët & Chandon, Mercier, Pol Roger. Cellar visits possible. Good moorings.

name: Châlons-en-Champagne
desc: Attractive town, sometimes called the 'Venice of Champagne' because of its many canals and bridges. Gothic church of Notre-Dame-en-Vaux. Good port de plaisance.

name: Vitry-le-François
desc: Junction town where several canals meet. Good provisioning point. Major waterway crossroads – routes diverge here towards the Rhine, the Saône via Champagne-Bourgogne, or continuing to Nancy.

name: Compiègne
desc: Splendid royal palace and forest. The Armistice of 1918 was signed nearby. Good moorings and facilities. Worth a long stop for the forest walks.

name: Montargis
desc: Pleasant canal town with many waterways passing through. Canal du Loing joins here. Pralines candy was invented here. Good moorings and provisioning.

name: Briare
desc: Famous for the Briare aqueduct – a 662m canal bridge carrying the Canal Latéral over the Loire, built by Gustave Eiffel. Remarkable spectacle. Good port de plaisance.

name: Nevers
desc: Capital of the Nièvre. Cathedral and ducal palace. Famous for its pottery (faïence). Good moorings. Motor racing circuit is here.

name: Digoin
desc: Junction of three canals – Canal du Centre, Canal Latéral à la Loire, and Canal de Roanne à Digoin. Splendid views of the Loire. Good facilities.

name: Chalon-sur-Saône
desc: Pleasant Burgundy town. End of the Bourbonnais route. Good port de plaisance facilities, fuel available. Nice old town to explore. Junction with the Saône.

name: Clamecy
desc: Attractive medieval town on the Yonne and Nivernais canal. Good moorings. The floating timber trade that once made the Nivernais famous started here.

name: Decize
desc: Southern terminus of the Canal de Nivernais at the Loire. Old town with 7th century crypt. Good moorings.

name: Laroche-Migennes
desc: Start of the Canal de Bourgogne, one of the most beautiful canal routes in France. Railway junction town. Excellent provisioning.

name: Tonnerre
desc: Attractive town with medieval hospital (Hôtel-Dieu). The famous Fosse Dionne spring is worth seeing. Comfortable moorings.

name: Montbard
desc: Birthplace of the naturalist Buffon. Close to the remarkable Cistercian abbey of Fontenay (UNESCO World Heritage Site). Good moorings.

name: Dijon
desc: The capital of Burgundy. The Palais des Ducs de Bourgogne contains an outstanding fine arts museum. Famous for mustard and Burgundy wines. Excellent facilities at the port de plaisance.

name: St-Jean-de-Losne
desc: Major junction where the Canal de Bourgogne meets the Saône. Renowned as a boating centre with a large marina. Annual waterways gathering. Excellent facilities for wintering and repairs.

name: Corre
desc: Start of the Petite Saône. Small town at the confluence of the Saône and Coney rivers. Peaceful setting.

name: Gray
desc: Attractive town on the Saône. 15th century Château de Gray houses a good local museum. Comfortable port de plaisance.

name: Mâcon
desc: Gateway to the Beaujolais wine region. Old bridge and Lamartine's birthplace. Lively riverside. Good moorings.

name: Tournus
desc: Remarkable Romanesque abbey church of St-Philibert. Beautiful town. Comfortable moorings and good restaurants.

name: Lyon
desc: France's second city. Magnificent setting at the confluence of the Rhône and Saône. Exceptional gastronomy – the bouchons lyonnais are unmissable. UNESCO World Heritage historic centre. Port de Plaisance at Confluence. Transition to the fast-flowing Rhône begins here.

name: Vienne
desc: Important Roman town with a well-preserved Roman theatre and Temple of Augustus and Livia. Excellent restaurant town (La Pyramide is legendary). Good moorings.

name: Valence
desc: Gateway to Provence. Famous for its nougat. Good port de plaisance. Nearby Hauterives has the extraordinary Palais Idéal of the Facteur Cheval.

name: Avignon
desc: The Palais des Papes – the largest Gothic building in the world. The famous 'Pont d'Avignon' (Pont Saint-Bénézet). Excellent port de plaisance on the Île de la Barthelasse. The Rhône current is strong here – take care.

name: Arles
desc: Roman amphitheatre and town. Van Gogh lived here. Gateway to the Camargue. Good moorings. Junction for the Petit Rhône route to the Camargue and Sète. Important for those choosing the alternate route to the Mediterranean.

name: Sète
desc: 'The Venice of Languedoc' – a lively fishing port and Mediterranean resort. End of the Canal du Rhône à Sète. Good facilities. Famous for its Joutes nautiques (water jousting) and mussels and oysters.

name: Lunel
desc: Attractive town. Good moorings. Famous for its Muscat wine.

name: Aigues-Mortes
desc: Magnificent 13th century walled town in the Camargue. Perfectly preserved medieval ramparts. Worth a long stop to explore the extraordinary fortifications.

name: Dunkerque
desc: Major Channel port. Departure/entry point for boats from UK's east coast. Good marina facilities. Known for the 1940 evacuation. Junction for multiple northern canal routes.

name: Calais
desc: Major cross-Channel ferry port. Entry point for boats from Kent. Good marina. Rodin's famous sculpture 'The Burghers of Calais' is in the town hall square.

name: Saint-Omer
desc: Attractive old town with fine Gothic cathedral. Famous for market gardens ('Les Watergangs'). Good moorings. A pleasant surprise for waterway explorers.

name: St-Valery-sur-Somme
desc: Charming harbour town at the mouth of the Somme. William the Conqueror set sail from here. Good moorings. Worth a visit especially for the wildlife of the Somme estuary.

name: Amiens
desc: The largest Gothic cathedral in France. The Hortillonnages (floating market gardens) are fascinating. Good port de plaisance. Jules Verne lived here.

name: Cambrai
desc: Famous for its linen (cambric/batiste) and for the first great tank battle (1917). Good moorings. Start of the Canal de St-Quentin.

name: Arras
desc: Fine Flemish Baroque squares (Grand'Place and Place des Héros). Outstanding Belfry. Significant WW1 history. Good facilities.

name: Givet
desc: Northern gateway on the Meuse, near the Belgian border. Fort Charlemont overlooks the town. Start of the Canal de la Meuse.

name: Charleville-Mézières
desc: Birthplace of the poet Rimbaud. The Place Ducale is a beautiful 17th century square. Good moorings. Puppet festival every 3 years.

name: Verdun
desc: The great WW1 battlefield. The Ossuaire de Douaumont and extensive battlefield memorials are essential visiting. Good moorings in the town centre.

name: Metz
desc: Cathedral of St Etienne has the largest area of stained glass windows in the world. Elegant city centre. Good port de plaisance on the Moselle.

name: Nancy
desc: The Place Stanislas is one of the finest baroque squares in Europe (UNESCO World Heritage Site). Art Nouveau architecture throughout the town. Good moorings.

name: Épinal
desc: Capital of the Vosges. Famous for its printed images. The basilica and town park are pleasant. Good moorings on the Canal des Vosges.

name: Bar-le-Duc
desc: Medieval upper town with fine Renaissance houses. Famous for its 'Brouilly' (seedless jam). Moorings on the Canal de la Marne au Rhin.

name: Strasbourg
desc: The capital of Alsace and seat of the European Parliament. The Cathedral of Notre-Dame is remarkable. The Petite France district is charming. Excellent port de plaisance. Junction of the Marne-Rhine canal and the Rhine.

name: Colmar
desc: 'The most Alsatian of Alsatian towns.' Beautifully preserved medieval and Renaissance town centre. The Unterlinden Museum contains Grünewald's masterpiece altarpiece. Good moorings on the Lauch. Excellent Alsace wines nearby.

name: Mulhouse
desc: Industrial city but with exceptional museums – the Cité de l'Automobile (largest car museum in the world). Entry point from the Rhine. Junction of the Canal du Rhône au Rhin (Branche Sud).

name: St-Malo
desc: Famous walled city. Birthplace of Jacques Cartier and Chateaubriand. Superb beaches. Excellent marina in the old town basin. Start/end of the Ille-et-Rance canal (Route 41 northern end).

name: Dinan
desc: One of the best-preserved medieval towns in Brittany. Ramparts, cobbled streets, half-timbered houses. The port is in the Rance river gorge below the town. Beautiful 30-minute walk up to the old town.

name: Rennes
desc: Capital of Brittany. Parliament building, fine art museum, lively student city. The canal passes through the city centre. Good moorings.

name: Redon
desc: Major waterway junction in Brittany. The Vilaine, the Nantes-Brest canal, and the Ille-et-Rance meet here. Good moorings and facilities. Charming old town.

name: Nantes
desc: Capital of Pays-de-la-Loire. The Château des Ducs de Bretagne. Jules Verne's birthplace. The remarkable Machines de l'Île. Good port de plaisance.

name: Royan
desc: Atlantic seaside resort at the mouth of the Gironde. Entry point for the Canal des Deux Mers. The rebuilt church of Notre-Dame is remarkable 1950s architecture. Good marina.

name: Bordeaux
desc: UNESCO World Heritage City. The 'Crescent' of 18th century buildings fronts the Garonne. Magnificent wine country surrounds the city. Good facilities on the Garonne quays.

name: Agen
desc: Capital of prunes (pruneaux d'Agen). The Canal de Garonne aqueduct carries the canal over the Garonne. Good moorings. Excellent market.

name: Toulouse
desc: The 'Pink City' – built of pink brick. Major university city. Start of the Canal du Midi (the original Riquet canal). The Port Saint-Sauveur is the junction. Excellent facilities.

name: Carcassonne
desc: The greatest surviving medieval fortified city in Europe (UNESCO World Heritage Site). The 12th century Cité is extraordinary. Good port de plaisance just outside the walls. One of the great stops of the Canal du Midi.

name: Béziers
desc: Cathedral on a hill above the Canal du Midi. The famous Écluses de Fonserannes – 9 locks in a staircase – just outside the town. Centre of the Languedoc wine region.

name: Agde
desc: The unique circular 'round lock' at the junction with the Hérault river (leave the canal for the sea via this lock at specific tidal times). Ancient town with a striking black basalt cathedral.

name: Fonserannes Locks
desc: The spectacular staircase of 9 locks (Écluses de Fonserannes) near Béziers – one of the most photographed engineering features of the Canal du Midi. Built by Pierre-Paul Riquet in the 17th century. Drops 21.5m in 300m.

name: Rochefort
desc: Historic naval town. The Corderie Royale (Royal Rope Walk) is a remarkable 17th century building. Good moorings. Start of the River Charente navigation.

name: Saintes
desc: Major Roman town. The 1st century Roman Arch of Germanicus. Amphitheatre and Arena. Good moorings on the Charente.

name: Angoulême
desc: Hilltop town with cathedral and remarkable ramparts with views. Now famous as the world capital of comics (Festival International de la Bande Dessinée). Good moorings below the old town.

name: Moissac
desc: Famous for its Romanesque cloisters (UNESCO World Heritage Site) – considered one of the finest in Europe. Aqueduct carries the Canal de Garonne over the Tarn. Good moorings.

name: Montauban
desc: Birthplace of Ingres. Fine 17th century brick town on the Tarn. Pont Vieux bridge is elegant. Moorings on the Tarn just below the aqueduct.

name: Port Lauragais
desc: Rest area and museum at the Col de Naurouze – the highest point of the Canal du Midi (189.3m). Pierre-Paul Riquet's monument is here. The canal descends both towards Toulouse and towards Sète from this point.

name: Bordeaux (Pont de Pierre)
desc: Tidal start — the Pont de Pierre (VERCLR 11.9 m at reference, ~4–5 m at PHMA spring high water). Passage under the bridge is governed by the tide; time your transit within 1–2 h of slack water. See the 🌊 Tidal section info when planning this route.

name: Portets
desc: Tidal Garonne. High-water offset from Bordeaux reference: roughly +30 min (coeff 45) to +50 min (coeff 100). No formal halte — lay alongside by arrangement only.

name: Cadillac
desc: Tidal Garonne. Minimum marnage ~3.5 m in étiage. Castle of Cadillac overlooks the river. High-water offset ~+50 min to +1 h 20 min relative to Bordeaux.

name: Langon
desc: Tidal Garonne, approaching the upper tidal limit (La Réole is the furthest tidal-influence point). Marnage drops to ~2.5 m. High-water offset ~+1 h 10 min to +1 h 50 min.

name: Castets-en-Dorthe (maritime)
desc: Junction with the Canal de Garonne. End of tidal Garonne navigation. Marnage ~1.5 m at étiage, tide not accused at coefficient 45. Gateway lock into the canal system.

name: Pouilly-en-Auxois Tunnel
desc: Canal de Bourgogne: 3,333m long tunnel at the summit. Max height 3.1m, max beam 3m. Longest navigable tunnel in France. Tow-through (électrique) by appointment. Allow 2–3 hours. Boats with wheelhouses may not pass.

name: Écluse de la Chapelle
desc: One of the 63 locks on the Ille-et-Rance canal (Liaison Manche-Océan). Automated operation. Typical of the shallow Brittany canals — leafy, pastoral setting.

name: Arzviller Inclined Plane (Plan incliné)
desc: Replaces 17 traditional locks on the Canal de la Marne au Rhin. A water-filled caisson carries boats up or down a 108.65m slope, descending 44.55m. Built 1969. One of the great engineering sights of European waterways. Advance booking required. VHF Ch 22.

name: Rogny-les-Sept-Écluses (historic)
desc: Historic seven-lock staircase on the Canal de Briare built by Sully (1605–1642). One of the oldest canal staircases in France — now a listed monument, no longer in use for navigation (replaced by a single modern bypass lock). Well worth stopping to visit. The village has a cruiser hire base.

name: Bollène Lock (Écluse de Bollène)
desc: One of the largest navigation locks in Europe on the Rhône: rise/fall of 23m. Integrated with the Donzère-Mondragon hydroelectric dam. VHF Ch 17. Approach with care — strong approach currents. Waiting pontoons both banks. Passage can take 45 minutes.

name: Avignon Lock (Écluse des Sorgues)
desc: Lock on the Rhône near Avignon — the gateway to Provence. 18m rise/fall. VHF Ch 17. Approach carefully in strong current. Below the lock is the famous Pont d'Avignon. Port de plaisance on the Île de la Barthelasse nearby.

name: Fonserannes Locks
desc: Nine-lock staircase (8 in regular use) near Béziers — the iconic image of the Canal du Midi. Built by Pierre-Paul Riquet in the 1680s. Drops 21.5m in 300m. A water slope (Pente d'Eau) added 1983 runs alongside. UNESCO World Heritage Site. Allow 1–2 hours.

name: Agde Round Lock (Écluse Ronde)
desc: The unique circular lock of Agde — only round lock on the Canal du Midi. Has three gates: one to the canal, one to the river Hérault, and one to the sea branch (Grau d'Agde). Built by Riquet in the 17th century. A remarkable curiosity and UNESCO World Heritage element. Tidal timing needed for the sea route.

name: Écluse de la Jonction (Decize)
desc: Junction lock at Decize where the Canal du Nivernais meets the Canal Latéral à la Loire. Two locks in quick succession. Below the lock is access to the Loire (currently unnavigable). Good moorings and provisioning at Decize. Major route choice point.

name: Écluse de l'Arsenal (Paris)
desc: Entry/exit lock for the Port de Plaisance de Paris-Arsenal on Canal Saint-Martin. Located just off Place de la Bastille. VHF Ch 10. Opening times restricted to daylight; advance booking essential for the marina. A memorable arrival to the heart of Paris by boat.

name: Vitry-le-François Lock (Canal-Marne Junction)
desc: Important junction lock where the Canal de la Marne au Rhin leaves the Canal latéral à la Marne at Vitry-le-François. Major waterway crossroads — routes diverge here towards Nancy/Strasbourg and Champagne-Bourgogne. VHF monitored. Good waiting pontoons.

name: Rennes Lock (Canal d'Ille-et-Rance)
desc: The lock as the Ille-et-Rance canal passes through central Rennes, the capital of Brittany. The canal runs through the city centre. Automated lock. Good moorings just beyond in the city.

name: Écluse de Stenay (Meuse)
desc: Lock on the Canal de la Meuse in the deep Ardennes forest. Very scenic — the river is flanked by wooded hills. The Meuse is one of the most beautiful rivers in France. Stenay has the famous Musée Européen de la Bière (European Beer Museum).

name: Écluse de la Presque'île (Chalon junction)
desc: The final lock of the Canal du Centre entering the Saône at Chalon-sur-Saône. End of the Bourbonnais route (414km, 149 locks from St-Mammès). A moment worth marking. The lock is directly above the Saône marina at Chalon.

name: Melun
desc: Historic town on a Seine island. 11th century church of Notre-Dame. Good port de plaisance. Vaux-le-Vicomte château — said to have inspired Versailles — is 6km away.

name: Moret-sur-Loing
desc: Perfectly preserved medieval walled town where the Loing meets the Seine. The painter Sisley lived and worked here. Good moorings. Junction with the Canal du Loing heading south (Route 10).

name: Bray-sur-Seine
desc: Pleasant small town on the Petite Seine. Pontoon moorings available. Good provisioning. The valley here is unspoilt and quiet — typical of the Petite Seine character.

name: Nogent-sur-Seine
desc: The principal town of the upper Seine between Montereau and Marcilly. Good moorings and provisioning. Birthplace of Paul Dubois the sculptor. The town is near the end of the navigable Petite Seine.

name: Sens
desc: The first Gothic cathedral in France — St-Étienne, begun c.1135. Its Treasury contains Thomas Becket's robes. Good port de plaisance on the Yonne. Fine 16th century timbered houses in the old town.

name: Villeneuve-sur-Yonne
desc: Charming walled town with two medieval gateways still standing. The church has a fine Renaissance portal. Comfortable moorings. A pleasant overnight stop on the Yonne between Sens and Joigny.

name: Bassin de la Villette (Paris)
desc: The largest artificial lake in Paris, connecting Canal Saint-Martin and Canal de l'Ourcq. Lively waterside cafés and restaurants. Good temporary moorings. The Parc de la Villette and Cité des Sciences are right here.

name: Nemours
desc: Attractive medieval town on the Canal du Loing. Château de Nemours houses a good local museum. The forest of Fontainebleau extends nearby. Good moorings — a pleasant overnight stop on the Bourbonnais route south.

name: Gien
desc: Famous for fine faïence pottery (visit the château museum and factory). The 15th century château overlooks the Loire. Good moorings on the canal quay. Excellent local wines — Coteaux du Giennois.

name: Cosne-Cours-sur-Loire
desc: Important Loire Valley town — once a major ironworking centre supplying the French navy. The Loire is wide and impressive here. Good moorings on the canal. The local Coteaux du Giennois wines are worth trying.

name: La Charité-sur-Loire
desc: Medieval pilgrimage town with a magnificent Romanesque priory (UNESCO World Heritage). The old bridge and riverside promenade are beautiful. Good moorings on the canal latéral. Famous as a 'Cité du Livre' (book town).

name: Vermenton
desc: Pleasant village on the Yonne with good moorings. Gateway to the spectacular Cure river gorge. The canal follows the Cure through wooded limestone cliffs. Canoe hire available. Good restaurant by the lock.

name: Arcy-sur-Cure
desc: Famous for the Grottes d'Arcy — prehistoric caves with ancient paintings (28,000 years old). The canal passes through beautiful gorge scenery here. A small quay allows a visit to the caves. One of the most scenic sections of the Nivernais.

name: Châtel-Censoir
desc: Attractive hilltop village above the Yonne. The 12th century collegiate church of St Potentien looks down on the canal. Good moorings. The canal leaves the Yonne valley shortly south of here into quieter countryside.

name: Corbigny
desc: Quiet Burgundian market town accessible from the canal. Good provisioning and moorings. The surrounding Morvan hills offer excellent walking. A good base for exploring quieter Burgundy away from the tourist routes.

name: Châtillon-en-Bazois
desc: Delightful small town on the Canal du Nivernais. The château overlooks the canal. One of the most charming stops on the quieter southern section of the Nivernais. Free moorings. Rich cattle-farming countryside.

name: Tanlay
desc: Worth stopping for the magnificent Château de Tanlay — one of the finest Renaissance châteaux in Burgundy. Free moorings at the nearby lock. The 17th century château has exceptional frescoes and is open to visitors. Not to be missed.

name: Ancy-le-Franc
desc: The Château d'Ancy-le-Franc is a masterpiece of French Renaissance architecture, built 1544. Its interior decoration is exceptional. Port de plaisance right by the château. A major highlight of the Canal de Bourgogne.

name: Pouilly-en-Auxois
desc: The summit town above the 3,333m Pouilly tunnel (see lk001). The summit pound at 378m altitude is beautiful. Boat tow through the tunnel must be booked in advance. A memorable high point of the Canal de Bourgogne.

name: Auxonne
desc: Historic garrison town where a young Napoleon Bonaparte was first posted as artillery officer in 1788 — the Musée Bonaparte tells the story. Good port de plaisance. Fine fortified town gates. A pleasant stop before joining the Saône.

name: Port-sur-Saône
desc: Small town on the Petite Saône between Corre and Gray. Comfortable moorings. The château and church are worth a brief visit. The Saône valley here is quiet and unspoilt — typical of the peaceful northern Petite Saône.

name: Pontailler-sur-Saône
desc: Small town between Gray and Auxonne on the Saône. Good moorings. Convenient overnight stop between the Petite Saône and the boating hub of St-Jean-de-Losne. The surrounding region produces excellent Burgundy wines.

name: Verdun-sur-le-Doubs
desc: Junction of the Saône and Doubs rivers. Famous fish stew town — the Poche (a local Saône fish stew) was allegedly invented here. Excellent moorings at the river junction. Access to the Canal du Centre. Worth a meal stop.

name: Seurre
desc: Pleasant Saône town with good moorings. Excellent local fish restaurants — perch, pike and bream from the Saône. The area produces fine Burgundy wines. Good provisioning. A classic peaceful Saône overnight stop.

name: Belleville-en-Beaujolais
desc: Gateway to the Beaujolais wine region. The cave cooperative on the quay offers wine tasting. Good moorings. Fine 12th century church. Excellent local restaurants. A great stop before or after Lyon on the Saône.

name: Tournon-sur-Rhône
desc: Attractive town facing Tain-l'Hermitage across the Rhône. The Hermitage vineyards are among the greatest in France. Renaissance château overlooks the river. Port de plaisance below the town. Outstanding wine tasting (Hermitage, Crozes-Hermitage). A highlight of the Rhône.

name: Montélimar
desc: Famous for its nougat made from local lavender honey and almonds. Good moorings at the capitainerie. The old town has a fine château. Strong current in the Rhône here. Excellent provisioning and nougat shopping.

name: Pont-Saint-Esprit
desc: Named for the magnificent 13th century stone bridge, one of the oldest on the Rhône. Good moorings. Interesting old quarter and fine museum. Just north of the dramatic Bollène lock (26m rise) — a good overnight stop before the ascent.

name: Orange
desc: The Roman theatre of Orange is the best-preserved in the world (UNESCO World Heritage). The Arc de Triomphe is equally impressive. Good moorings. Châteauneuf-du-Pape vineyards are just 12km south — unmissable for wine lovers.

name: Lille
desc: Capital of French Flanders. The Grand'Place and Vieux Lille are beautiful. Exceptional Flemish art in the Palais des Beaux-Arts. France's best Sunday market (Marché de Wazemmes). Good moorings on the Canal de la Deûle through the city.

name: Douai
desc: Famous for its carillon of 62 bells — concerts every Saturday. The Musée de la Chartreuse has outstanding French paintings. Belfry is a UNESCO World Heritage site. Good moorings. The coalfields history of the surrounding area is visible throughout.

name: Valenciennes
desc: Important cultural city — the Musée des Beaux-Arts has paintings by Rubens and Van Dyck (the city produced the sculptor Carpeaux). End of the Liaison Dunkerque-Escaut navigation. Good moorings at the southern end of the canal.

name: Aire-sur-la-Lys
desc: Attractive Flemish town on the River Lys. 17th century Town Hall with fine belfry (UNESCO World Heritage). Good moorings. Junction of the Canal d'Aire and the Lys navigation. An authentic Flemish market town off the main tourist trail.

name: Messac-Guipry
desc: Twin villages on opposite banks of the Vilaine connected by a suspension bridge. One of the best haltes on the Liaison Manche-Océan. Excellent restaurants and provisioning. Very popular overnight stop on the Brittany canals.

name: Blain
desc: Pleasant town on the Canal de Nantes à Brest. The ruined Château de la Groulais dominates. Good moorings. The surrounding countryside is typical Breton bocage. An authentic town away from the tourist circuit.

name: Laval
desc: Capital of Mayenne. The medieval old town and castle above the river are impressive. Birthplace of the Douanier Rousseau — good museum. Good moorings on the Mayenne. The river navigation through Laval is particularly scenic.

name: Le Mans
desc: Famous for the 24-hour motor race, but the old city (Le Vieux Mans) with its Gallo-Roman walls and medieval streets is equally remarkable. The Cathedral has a superb nave. End of the River Sarthe navigation. Good moorings below the old town.

name: Berry-au-Bac
desc: Junction of the Canal latéral à l'Aisne with the Canal des Ardennes. Good halte fluviale. Historic Chemin des Dames battlefields nearby.

name: Soissons
desc: Major town on the Aisne with a splendid cathedral. Good mooring at the halte fluviale. Well-equipped town with all facilities.

name: Vic-sur-Aisne
desc: Pleasant small town. Halte fluviale with water and electricity. Castle ruins overlooking the river.

name: Attichy
desc: Quiet halt on the approach to Compiègne. Basic facilities.

name: Compiègne
desc: Royal city with a magnificent château. Good port de plaisance. Junction with the Canal de l'Oise à l'Aisne. Nearby Compiègne forest was site of 1918 armistice signing.

name: Vieux-lès-Asfeld
desc: Northern terminus of the Canal latéral à l'Aisne, junction with the Canal des Ardennes. Limited facilities.

name: Abbécourt
desc: Southern end of the Canal de l'Oise à l'Aisne, junction with the River Oise. Limited facilities.

name: Noyon
desc: Fine medieval cathedral city. Halte fluviale close to the town centre. Birthplace of John Calvin. Good provisioning.

name: Cuts
desc: Small village with a halte fluviale. Quiet overnight stop.

name: Sinceny
desc: Village halt. Nearby château. Connects to the Canal de Saint-Quentin.

name: Condé-sur-Marne
desc: Eastern terminus of the Canal de l'Oise à l'Aisne. Junction with the Marne river. Limited facilities.

name: Mulhouse
desc: Large industrial city in Alsace. Port de plaisance with good facilities. Excellent museums including the famous automobile museum. Junction at Niffer with the Rhine.

name: Dannemarie
desc: Small Alsatian town. Halte fluviale. Market town with provisioning.

name: Montbéliard
desc: Historic Franche-Comté city. Good port de plaisance. Château des Ducs de Wurtemberg dominates the skyline. Peugeot was founded nearby.

name: Besançon
desc: UNESCO World Heritage city in a dramatic meander of the Doubs. Vauban citadel, fine cathedral. Good halte fluviale. Birthplace of Victor Hugo.

name: Dole
desc: Charming old capital of Franche-Comté on the Doubs. Good halte fluviale in the old canal basin. Birthplace of Louis Pasteur. Fine arcaded streets.

name: St-Jean-de-Losne
desc: The 'crossroads of the canals' — junction of Canal du Rhône au Rhin, Canal de Bourgogne, River Saône. Excellent port facilities. Major chandlery and boat services. Annual boat festival.

name: Arles
desc: Ancient Roman city at the Rhône delta. UNESCO World Heritage. Good port. Amphitheatre, arena, van Gogh connections. Junction of Grand Rhône and Petit Rhône.

name: St-Gilles
desc: End of the Petit Rhône navigation. Junction with the Canal du Rhône à Sète. Romanesque abbey church. Good halte fluviale.

name: Pont-à-Bar
desc: Southern junction of the Canal des Ardennes with the Meuse. Small village. Locks begin here heading north.

name: Sedan
desc: Major town with a massive feudal château — the largest in Europe. Halte fluviale. Historic site of the 1870 Franco-Prussian War battle.

name: Rethel
desc: Pleasant market town on the Aisne. Good halte fluviale. Church of St Nicolas. Known for andouillette sausage.

name: Vouziers
desc: Small town in the Aisne valley. Halte fluviale with basic facilities. Gateway to the Argonne forest.

name: Vieux-lès-Asfeld
desc: Northern terminus of the Canal des Ardennes, junction with the Canal latéral à l'Aisne. Limited facilities.

name: Vitry-le-François
desc: Start of Canal entre Champagne et Bourgogne. Also junction with Canal de la Marne au Rhin and lateral Marne canal. Good port de plaisance. Reconstructed after WWII bombing.

name: St-Dizier
desc: Industrial town in the Haute-Marne. Halte fluviale. Canal de la Blaise junction. Reasonable provisioning.

name: Chaumont
desc: Prefecture of Haute-Marne. Good port de plaisance in the basin. Impressive railway viaduct. Annual international poster and graphic design festival.

name: Langres
desc: Summit level town perched on a plateau at 475m. Beautiful medieval walled city. Nearby Liez reservoir feeds the canal. Birthplace of Denis Diderot. Excellent cheeses.

name: Gray
desc: Old town on the Saône with fine Renaissance hôtel de ville. Halte fluviale. Junction area with the Saône. Good provisioning.

name: Maxilly-sur-Saône
desc: Southern terminus where the canal joins the Saône. Small village. Junction with the River Saône navigation.

name: Gondrexange
desc: Western junction of the Canal de la Sarre with the Canal de la Marne au Rhin. Small village.

name: Sarrebourg
desc: Main town on the Canal de la Sarre. Good halte fluviale. Chagall stained glass window in the chapel. Moselle valley gateway.

name: Fénétrange
desc: Medieval village with a château. Halte fluviale. One of the most picturesque stops on the canal.

name: Sarreguemines
desc: Border town at the German frontier. Good port de plaisance. Famous faience (earthenware) museum. Junction with German waterways.

name: Strasbourg
desc: Capital of Alsace and seat of the European Parliament. Excellent port de plaisance in the city centre. Cathedral, Petite France district. Major provisioning. International city with great restaurants.

name: Offendorf
desc: Village on the Canal du Rhône au Rhin Branche Nord. Halte fluviale. Good base for exploring the Rhine flood plain forest.

name: Rhinau
desc: Southern end of the Canal du Rhône au Rhin Branche Nord. Junction with the Grand Canal d'Alsace. Ferry crossing to Germany. Small village with halte fluviale.

name: Châteaulin
desc: Main town on the western section of the Nantes-Brest Canal. Good port de plaisance. Salmon river. Market town with facilities.

name: Châteauneuf-du-Faou
desc: Hilltop village above the canal. Beautiful Breton landscape. Basic halte fluviale.

name: Carhaix-Plouguer
desc: Market town at the highest point of the Nantes-Brest Canal. Good facilities. Celtic festival Vieilles Charrues held here annually.

name: Gouarec
desc: Village where the Blavet river begins. Halte fluviale. Beautiful wooded gorges. Junction with the Blavet river downstream.

name: Mûr-de-Bretagne
desc: Village near the Guerlédan reservoir — the largest lake in Brittany, but the section through is unnavigable. Detour by road necessary.

name: St-Nazaire
desc: Industrial port at the Loire estuary. WWII submarine pens. Massive shipyard. Limited facilities for pleasure craft. Start of Loire navigation.

name: Ancenis
desc: Town on the Loire with medieval château. Halte fluviale. Muscadet wine country. Good provisioning.

name: Angers
desc: Magnificent city on the Maine river. Port de plaisance. Black-and-white striped château with the famous Apocalypse Tapestry (14th century). Major wine region: Anjou, Muscadet, Saumur.

name: Nantes
desc: Capital of pays de Loire. Fine château des Ducs de Bretagne. Excellent port facilities at the marina. Port de l'Erdre and Canal de la Martinière junction.

name: Sallèles-d'Aude
desc: Junction of the Canal de la Robine with the Canal du Midi. Roman oppidum nearby. Wine country.

name: Narbonne
desc: Ancient city that was once on the coast. Cathedral, Roman Capitol. Good port de plaisance on the canal. All facilities. Excellent local wine and food.

name: Port-la-Nouvelle
desc: Mediterranean port at the end of the Canal de la Robine. Industrial but has a marina. Beach nearby. End of navigation.

name: Chauny
desc: Northern terminus of the Canal latéral à l'Oise. Junction with the Canal de Saint-Quentin. Halte fluviale.

name: Pontoise
desc: Old town at the confluence of the Oise with the Seine. Halte fluviale. Impressionist painting connections. Good provisioning.

name: Canal Saint-Martin
desc: The romantic canal in east Paris with 9 locks, iron footbridges and tree-lined quays. Arty, vibrant neighbourhood cafés and boutiques. Enters the underground covered section near République.

name: Pantin
desc: Canal de l'Ourcq terminus area north of Paris. Cultural regeneration zone. Halte fluviale. Access to Parc de la Villette.

name: Nogent-sur-Seine
desc: Pleasant town on a loop of the Seine. Good halte fluviale. Champagne wine country begins here. Nuclear power station visible downstream.

name: Romilly-sur-Seine
desc: Industrial town. Halte fluviale. Champagne region border. Provisioning available.

name: Troyes
desc: Former capital of Champagne, famous for its half-timbered medieval centre shaped like a Champagne cork. Excellent port de plaisance. Good shopping, restaurants, famous factory outlet shopping nearby.

name: Calais
desc: Major cross-Channel ferry port. Good port de plaisance in the old town basin. Rodin's Burghers of Calais sculpture. Excellent provisioning. Popular departure point for English canal boats.

name: Saint-Omer
desc: Historic Flemish town with a fine Gothic cathedral and extensive marshes (Marais Audomarois). Good port de plaisance. Junction with the River Aa.

name: Watten
desc: Junction of the Canal de Calais with the River Aa. Small town. End of the Canal de Calais navigation.

name: Gravelines
desc: Fortified harbour town at the mouth of the Aa. Vauban fortifications. Good stopping place. Nuclear power station nearby.

name: Watten
desc: Junction with the Canal de Calais. Small village. Ruined Benedictine abbey on the hill.

name: Saint-Omer
desc: End of the River Aa navigation. Junction with the Canal de Calais. Attractive Flemish town with fine cathedral. Spectacular marshland landscape.

name: Aire-sur-la-Lys
desc: Start of the River Lys navigation. Fine Grande Place with Flemish architecture. Good halte fluviale.

name: Armentières
desc: Town famous from the WWI song. Good halte fluviale. Busy industrial town. Junction area with Belgian waterways nearby.

name: Deûlémont
desc: End of the River Lys. Junction with the Canal de la Deûle and access to Lille. Quiet village.

name: Arleux
desc: Northern terminus of the Canal du Nord. Junction with the Canal de Sensée. Garlic capital of northern France — annual garlic festival.

name: Péronne
desc: Medieval citadel town on the Somme. Excellent Historial de la Grande Guerre museum. Halte fluviale.

name: Ham
desc: Town on the Somme plain. Halte fluviale. Canal connects to the Somme navigation here.

name: Cambrai
desc: Old fortified city. Good halte fluviale. Birthplace of the cambric fabric. Famous for WWI tank battle. Junction with Canal de la Sensée.

name: Saint-Quentin
desc: Major town with a fine Gothic collegiate church. Good port de plaisance. Canal tunnel nearby at Riqueval — tug service through 5.7km tunnel.

name: Chauny
desc: Southern end of the Canal de Saint-Quentin. Junction with the Canal latéral à l'Oise. Good facilities.

name: Amiens
desc: Cathedral city on the Somme — the largest Gothic cathedral in France. Good port de plaisance in the floating gardens (Hortillonnages). Excellent restaurants and market.

name: Sierck-les-Bains
desc: Northern end of the River Moselle navigation. Pretty medieval village dominated by a château. Good halte fluviale. Luxembourg border nearby.

name: Thionville
desc: Industrial city but with a good port de plaisance. Steel industry heritage. Junction for access to Luxembourg waterways.

name: Toul
desc: Walled medieval city with a lovely cathedral and cloisters. Good halte fluviale. Ring of Vauban fortifications. Junction with the Canal de la Marne au Rhin.

name: Bar-le-Duc
desc: Handsome old upper town with a remarkable Renaissance street. Good halte fluviale. Famous for redcurrant jam (groseille épépinée). Canal descends the Ornain valley.

name: Nancy
desc: Baroque city with the magnificent Place Stanislas (UNESCO). Good port de plaisance on the Meurthe. Fine arts museum, art nouveau architecture. Major provisioning.

name: Épinal
desc: Prefecture of the Vosges. Good port de plaisance. Famous for colourful naive printed images (Imagerie d'Épinal). Basilica of Saint-Maurice. Excellent forêt des Vosges walking.

name: Bains-les-Bains
desc: Spa town in the Vosges. Small halte fluviale. Thermal baths open to visitors. Quiet and wooded.

name: Fontenoy-le-Château
desc: Beautiful village at the foot of the Vosges. Halte fluviale. Canal enters the Saône plain here. Embroidery tradition.

name: Basel (Bâle)
desc: End of the Rhine navigation. Major Swiss city and port. Excellent art museums (Fondation Beyeler, Kunstmuseum). Junction of Swiss and German Rhine waterways.

name: Redon
desc: Canal junction town — meeting point of the Vilaine, Nantes-Brest Canal, and the Blavet. Good port de plaisance. Gateway to the Breton waterways. Medieval abbey.

name: Josselin
desc: Spectacular medieval château reflected in the canal. One of the most beautiful stops in Brittany. Good halte fluviale. Town of doll museum. Market town.

name: Redon
desc: Eastern start of the Nantes à Brest / Erdre section. Junction with the Vilaine. Good port de plaisance.

name: Nort-sur-Erdre
desc: Charming town on the Erdre. Good halte fluviale. Vineyard area. Pleasant day trip from Nantes.

name: Laval
desc: Prefecture of the Mayenne. Good port de plaisance below the medieval château. Birthplace of the Douanier Rousseau painter. Provisioning.

name: Sablé-sur-Sarthe
desc: Attractive town with a château and abbey. Good port de plaisance. Famous for Sablé biscuits (sablés). Solesmes monastery nearby — Gregorian chant.
